sample.address.message: Your company · Street and number · City, postcode
sample.address.note: The sample content of the starter templates below goes into the email, so it is written for its readers. This line stands in a footer until the workspace sets its postal address.

sample.weekly.headline: A headline that says what's inside this week

sample.weekly.intro.message: Hi {firstName}, two or three sentences on what this issue covers and why it matters to the reader.
sample.weekly.intro.note: firstName is the tag that prints the reader's first name (or the fallback word for "there")

sample.weekly.articleAlt: Describe the {n, select, 1 {first} 2 {second} other {next}} article's image
sample.weekly.articleLine: One or two sentences that make people want to read the rest.
sample.update.headline: Announce the one thing that changed
sample.update.body: Hi {firstName}, say what's new, who it's for and what they can do with it today. Keep it to one idea so the button has one job.
sample.plain.write: Write this the way you would write to one person: what happened, what you learned, and what you would like them to do next.
sample.plain.detail: A second paragraph with the detail. Short paragraphs read well on phones.
sample.announce.headline: One big announcement
sample.announce.lead: Hi {firstName}, lead with the news, then the one detail that makes it matter.
sample.announce.detail: Add the date, the price or the deadline if there is one.
sample.grid.intro: Hi {firstName}, a sentence that ties the products together: a season, a sale, a new collection.
sample.digest.intro: Hi {firstName}, here's what's new on the blog this week.

sample.digest.readPost.note: the button under each post of the feed
